events.note: Query: COMMAND 599 (Jupiter) over 2026-10-21 03:37-03:41; the Lunar Apogee is the osculating apogee, which is not a Horizons body and Horizons cannot list it, so its longitude here is Swiss Ephemeris SE_OSCU_APOG, the body the pipeline uses, bounded independently: the apogee direction computed from Horizons geocentric Moon state vectors (COMMAND 301, EPHEM_TYPE='VECTORS', CENTER='500@399', REF_PLANE='ECLIPTIC', VEC_CORR='NONE', TIME_TYPE='UT', eccentricity vector with GM of Earth plus Moon) is 268.49734 in the J2000 ecliptic at 03:39 UT against Swiss Ephemeris' 268.49741, and carrying it to the ecliptic of date with IAU 2006 precession (0.3747) and nutation (0.0023) agrees with Swiss Ephemeris to 0.0003 degrees. GM of Earth alone moves it 10 degrees, so the apogee is defined by that convention, not by Horizons. Forms when its last leg, the Jupiter-Lunar Apogee trine, enters the 6 degree orb: Jupiter 142.8752 and 142.8753, apogee 268.8760 and 268.8741, separation 126.0008 at 03:38 UT and 125.9988 at 03:39 UT. The other five legs are already in orb at 03:39: Jupiter-Chiron trine (COMMAND 599, '2060;', 0.30 degrees inside orb), Chiron-Lunar Apogee trine (5.05 inside), Moon-Jupiter opposition (COMMAND 301, 599, in orb from 2026-10-20 07:01 UT), Moon-Chiron sextile (301, '2060;', from 02:11 UT) and Moon-Lunar Apogee sextile (from 02:55 UT). The Moon opposes Jupiter and sextiles the other two, so it is the focal body. The separation changes 0.002 degrees a minute, so the 0.001 degree bound on the apogee fixes this boundary to within one minute, which is the fixture's tolerance; the Horizons-only boundary below is exact to the minute.

Every other leg stays in orb through 14:22: the Moon-Lunar Apogee sextile until 15:24 UT and the Moon-Chiron sextile until 17:26 UT.
